newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates seen stable, Indian down.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates seen stable, Indian down.

text.p: Cotton rates are likely to be stable in Pakistan next week on buying by mills, but could weaken in India on selling by traders, dealers said on Friday.
Dealers said Pakistani prices stayed steady this week amid selective buying by mills and would hover at similar levels until arrivals from the 1997/98 (July-June) crop accelerate.
They said there was demand for new and old crop cotton, but buying was not aggressive because mills were short of funds.
"For the time being prices will remain at these levels, but will dip once the arrival of fresh supplies picks up," dealer Kishan Chand said.
Dealer Shamimul Haq said the moisture level was high in new crop arrivals. "It's not fully mature yet," he added.
About 150,000 bales of unsold cotton remain from the 1996/97 crop, including 50,000 bales of fine quality, dealers said.

In India, local cotton prices fell this week, traders said, adding that the progress of monsoon rains in cotton-producing states had prompted selling by traders, they said.

"The progress of monsoon rains has been satisfactory and brightened the prospects for the 1997/98 (October/September) crop," one trader said. "But it's too early to predict the size of the new crop at this juncture."
The cotton crop in 1996/97 has been estimated at 16.78 million 170-kg bales, up from 16.27 million the previous year.

In spot, Bengal-deshi slid 5.0 rupees to 1,025/1,050 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), while Punjab saw-ginned lost 20 rupees to 1,825/1,860 rupees per maund. F-414 fell 15/20 rupees to 2,050/2,075 rupees per maund.
Among Gujarat varieties, Kalyan fell 100 rupees to 13,800/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Superior variety long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 lost 500 rupees to 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy.
